title: REALHOP: Rethinking Multi-Hop Reasoning Evaluation via Behavioral Auditing
abstract: arXiv:2609.36984v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Complex questions often require multi-hop reasoning that connects facts distributed across sources or distant regions of a long context through intermediate steps. Benchmarks commonly evaluate this ability with questions built around predefined reasoning chains, treating a correct answer as evidence that the intended composition was used. Yet answer correctness alone leaves open whether success depends on the evidence associated with each intended step: models may instead rely on memorized associations, shorter paths, or partial evidence. We examine this dependence using the Behavioral Necessity Rate (BNR), which measures how often targeted evidence removal prevents answer recovery on initially correct instances. Across five existing benchmarks, panel-mean BNR ranges from 16.6% to 48.9%, exposing a substantial gap between annotated structure and observed dependence. Guided by this diagnosis, we introduce REALHOP, a diagnose-construct-ver

translated_title: REALHOP：通过行为审计重新思考多跳推理评估
translated_abstract: arXiv:2609.36984v1 公告类型：新论文 摘要：复杂问题通常需要多跳推理，即通过中间步骤连接分布在多个来源或长上下文中相距遥远区域的事实。基准测试通常通过围绕预定义推理链构建的问题来评估这种能力，并将正确答案视为模型使用了预期推理组合的证据。然而，仅凭答案正确性无法确定成功是否依赖于与每个预期步骤相关联的证据：模型可能转而依赖记忆中的关联、更短的路径或部分证据。我们使用行为必要性率来检验这种依赖性，该指标衡量在初始回答正确的实例上，移除目标证据后阻止答案恢复的频率。在五个现有基准测试中，面板平均BNR范围为16.6%至48.9%，揭示了标注结构与实际观察到的依赖性之间的显著差距。基于这一诊断结果，我们提出了REALHOP，一个诊断-构建-验证（原文摘要在此处截断）……
tldr: 该论文提出行为必要性率（BNR）指标，通过移除目标证据来审计模型是否真正依赖预期的多跳推理链证据，发现五个现有基准中BNR仅为16.6%至48.9%，暴露了标注结构与实际依赖之间的巨大差距，并据此提出新的REALHOP评估基准。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes the Behavioral Necessity Rate (BNR) to audit whether models' correct answers on multi-hop reasoning benchmarks truly depend on the intended evidence per step, revealing that panel-mean BNR ranges only from 16.6% to 48.9% across five benchmarks, and introduces REALHOP, a new benchmark guided by this behavioral diagnosis.
